sentences.text:
2. The appellant is the defendant who has lost his case from both the Courts below.
3. The plaintiff/ respondent No.1 filed a suit for declaration, partition and separate possession by contending inter alia that the plaintiff/ respondent No.1, the defendant No.1/ appellant and defendant No.2/respondent No.2 are real brothers.
They and their father had ancestral properties which were acquired for Indira Sagar Project and accordingly, all of them were dispossessed.

From the compensation amount received in lieu of acquisition of the ancestral property, the lands situated in village Markala, Tahsil Pandhana, District Khandwa were purchased in the name of their father.
A house was also constructed over 2300 square feet of land.

The lands situated in village Balrampur were purchased in the name of plaintiff and defendants No.1 and 2 and a house was also constructed from the compensation amount received in lieu of acquisition of their ancestral property.

The father of the plaintiff and defendants No.1 and 2, namely, Shri Ghasiram died on 30/07/2013 and after his death, the names of the plaintiff as well as the defendants No.1 and 2 were recorded in revenue record in respect of lands situated in village Markala which is shown in schedule-A.
Earlier the defendant No.2 - Hare Singh was exclusively cultivating the said land, however after the death of Ghasiram, he left 4 acres of land and gave separate possession to the plaintiff.

Khasra No.465 area 0.800 hectare and khasra No. 466/1 area 0.800 hectare which are situated in village Markala jointly belongs to all the three brothers but the land has not been partitioned in the revenue records and even the house has also not been partitioned.

It was also pleaded that the property shown in schedule-B is in possession of Haresingh/ defendant No.2 and since the plaintiff as well as the defendant No.1 were in Government job, therefore, they were not in a position to personally cultivate the land situated in village Balrampur.
Therefore the defendant No.2 was cultivating the land on behalf of all the co-sharers.
However, it was alleged that the lands mentioned in schedule - A and B are jointly recorded in the names of plaintiff as well as the defendants No.1 and 2.
Accordingly, it was claimed that the plaintiff as well as the defendants No.1 and 2 have 1/3rd share in the lands in dispute.
The plaintiff had requested the defendants No.1 and 2 to partition the land and get the names mutated but the defendant No.1 started picking up quarrel.

The compensation which was awarded in lieu of acquisition was enhanced and the enhanced amount was deposited but the defendant No.1 got his name recorded as a nominee and thus, it was prayed that the plaintiff has 1/3rd share in the land in dispute and accordingly, he is entitled for partition of the same and separate possession.
4. By way of amendment, it was also incorporated that the property in dispute was purchased from the compensation which was received in lieu of the acquisition of the ancestral property.
Late Ghasiram had never executed a Will dated 15/06/2010.
The so called Will is a sham and forged document.

5. The defendant No.1/ appellant filed his written statement and admitted that the land in dispute was purchased from the compensation amount which was received in lieu of acquisition of the Genda Lal vs Babulal on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84409936/
2 ancestral property of Ghasiram.
However, it was claimed that Ghasiram has expired on 30/07/2013.
He had executed a Will dated 15-16/06/2010 and all the legal representatives got share as per the Will.
It was denied that the plaintiff has not been given any share in the lands situated in village Markala.
It was denied that the plaintiff is cultivating 0.800 hectare of land forming part of khasra No.465 and 466/1 respectively.
By way of amendment, it was incorporated that Late Ghasiram has executed a Will in favour of defendant No.1 which was got registered on 16/06/2010.
6. The defendant No.2 also filed written statement and he also admitted the nature of the land in dispute.
He also claimed that Ghasiram had executed a Will.
In special pleading, the defendant No.2 also claimed that the property in dispute is not the ancestral property but it is the self-acquired property.

7. The Trial Court after framing issues and recording evidence, decreed the suit and declared that the plaintiff as well as the defendants No.1 and 2 have 1/3rd share in the property in dispute as well as the plaintiff is entitled to get the land partitioned and is also entitled for a separate possession.

8. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court, the appellant/defendant No.1 preferred an appeal which too has been dismissed by the First Appellate Court by the impugned judgment.

9. Challenging the judgments and decrees passed by the Courts below, it is submitted by the counsel for the appellant that the Courts below failed to see that the plaintiff/ respondent No.1 had admitted that the land in dispute is the self-acquired property of Ghasiram, and therefore any contrary finding with regard to the nature of the land in dispute is erroneous.

Even otherwise, the Will was acted upon therefore, the plaintiff is estopped from challenging the Will and accordingly, proposed the following substantial questions of law:-
(A) Whether, the plaintiff admitting his father Ghasiram to be the owner of the disputed property is stopped from challenging the property to the ancestral property?
(B) Whether, Late Ghasiram has right to execute registered will dated 15/16.06.2010 Ex.D/1?

(C) Whether, the registered will deed dt.
15/16.06.2010 Ex.D/1 is legally proved by the defendants No.1 & 2?
(D) Whether, the plaintiff and defendant acted upon the will Ex.D/1 are the plaintiff has no right for partition?

(E) Whether, the findings of the courts below is perverse?"
10. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant.
11.

The plaintiff in paragraph 1 has specifically stated that the ancestral lands of Ghasiram situated in village Sonpura, Tehsil Harsood, District Khandwa were acquired as they had come in submergence area of Indira Sagar Project.

It was further pleaded in paragraph 2 that from the Genda Lal vs Babulal on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84409936/

sentences.text: compensation amount received in lieu of acquisition of the ancestral land situated in village Sonpura, the lands in dispute situated in village Markala and Balrampur were purchased.

The land situated in village Markala was purchased in the name of their father Ghasiram whereas the lands situated in village Balrampur were purchased in the name of plaintiff as well as the defendants No.1 and 2.

Thus, according to the plaintiff, since the lands in dispute were purchased from the compensation amount received in lieu of acquisition of their ancestral property, therefore the nature of the land in dispute shall remain to be ancestral.
The aforesaid pleadings have been categorically admitted by the defendants No.1 and 2 by filing their separate written statements.
Thus, the ancestral land situated in village Sonpura, Tehsil Harsood, District Khandwa was acquired is an undisputed fact.

The lands in dispute i.e, situated in village Markala and Balrampur, Tehsil Pandhana, District Khandwa were purchased from the compensation amount received in lieu of acquisition of the ancestral land situated in village Sonpura is also an undisputed fact.
Thus, in the considered opinion of this Court, the nature of the land in dispute would continue to remain as ancestral land.
12. Under these circumstances, it is clear that Ghasiram had no right to execute any Will.
Even otherwise, the burden is on the propounder of the Will to remove all the suspicious circumstances which are attached to a Will.
In view of the specific admission made by the defendants No.1 and 2 that the land in dispute was purchased from the compensation amount of ancestral property
, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Courts below did not commit any mistake by holding that the lands in dispute are the ancestral properties.

13. It is next contended by the counsel for the appellant that the respondent No.1 by making certain admissions in his evidence has categorically admitted that the Will was acted upon and therefore the respondent No.1/ plaintiff is estopped from challenging the Will.
14.
Considered the submissions made by the counsel for the appellant.
15. This Court has gone through the evidence of Babulal (PW-1).
Babulal has specifically stated that he is in possession of 4 acres of land whereas only 3 acres of land has been given in the Will in question.
He has also questioned the unequal distribution of land in the Will.

In the cross-examination, Babulal (PW-1) had admitted that the property was purchased in the name of Ghasiram but admitted that the property in question was the self-acquired property of his father and once again claimed that it is an ancestral property.
Further suggestion was given that the property in dispute was purchased from the compensation awarded in lieu of acquisition of ancestral property which was admitted.
16. From the plain reading of the entire evidence of Babulal (PW-1), it cannot be held that Babulal (PW-1) had ever acted upon the Will.
On the contrary, it is his specific statement that he is in possession of 4 acres of land whereas only 3 acres of land has been given in the Will.

17. Furthermore, it is well established principle of law that this Court while exercising powers under Section 100 of CPC cannot interfere with the concurrent findings of fact recorded by the Courts below.

In spite of that, this Court has gone through the evidence of Babulal (PW-1) and no perversity Genda Lal vs Babulal on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84409936/
4 could be pointed out by the counsel for the appellant in the concurrent findings of fact recorded by both the Courts below.
18.
At this stage, it is submitted by the counsel for the appellant that the Executing Court/ Authority may be directed to partition the land in accordance with the quality of the land.
19. This submission made by the counsel for the appellant cannot be considered at this stage because the stage of execution of decree has not come.
At present, this Court is required to look into the findings given by the Courts below.
20. No other argument is advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

21. As no substantial question of law arises in the present appeal, therefore the judgment and decree dated 16/02/2018 passed by Fifth Additional District Judge, Khandwa, District Khandwa (M.P.) in RCA No.200015/2015 arising out of the judgment and decree dated 19/10/2015 passed by Fourth Civil Judge Class-1, Khandwa (M.P.), are hereby affirmed.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 22. The appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
